title: SecondFi Said the Yoroi Breach Was 'Around $2.4M, 16M ADA.' SlowMist's Cos Said on X That After Tracking the Attackers' Wallet Flows, 'Users Have Likely Lost Over $20M, 129M ADA Plus Other Tokens.' The Breach Is at the Wallet-Generation Layer — Every Wallet Created Through the Affected Software Is at Risk (23-24 June 2026)
narrative: On 23 June 2026, SecondFi — the Cardano ecosystem self-custody 'neofinance' wallet formerly known as Yoroi — disclosed a security breach in which attackers exploited a vulnerability in the platform's proprietary Cardano wallet-generation software, draining ADA, tokens, and NFTs from user accounts. SecondFi's preliminary official estimate put the loss at 'around 16 million ADA, worth roughly $2.4 million at the time of the incident.' The platform paused services, entered maintenance mode, and said it was finalizing an independent technical review with a leading blockchain security firm. On 24 June, SlowMist founder Cos (Yu Xian) said on X that after tracking the attacker's fund flows and wallet activity overnight, he had identified two suspected attacker addresses and concluded that 'the users of this wallet have likely lost over $20 million, as much as 129 million ADA plus other tokens, many times SecondFi's official estimate.' Cos later noted the transaction pattern suggested the attacker may have obtained a batch of mnemonic phrases or private keys before moving funds over many hours, with transfers moving from larger to smaller amounts. SecondFi is the successor to Yoroi (launched in 2018 by EMURGO, one of Cardano's three founding entities), rebranded and shipped as version 10.0.3 on 7 June 2026. The platform had positioned itself as a self-custody 'neofinance' application with Visa integrations, used by more than a million ADA holders. The breach is at the wallet-generation layer, not the smart-contract layer — meaning every wallet created through the affected software is potentially at risk, not just the wallets that interacted with a particular contract. The transaction pattern (larger-to-smaller transfers, sustained over many hours) is consistent with a mnemonic-phrase or private-key batch compromise at the wallet-creation step.

analysis: Three findings structure this story, and each one names a specific evidentiary layer that the prior corporate-disclosure articles (T1 Energy / Trina Solar 16 June, WiseTech / Richard White 23 June) did not contain. First, the 8x gap between SecondFi's $2.4M / 16M ADA official figure and SlowMist's $20M / 129M ADA independent figure is the load-bearing contradiction. SecondFi's own on-chain review put the figure at ~16M ADA; SlowMist's independent on-chain analysis of two suspected attacker addresses puts the figure at 129M ADA plus other tokens. The roughly eightfold gap is unresolved as of publication. SecondFi has not yet released a final technical report or a detailed compensation plan, and the 'official number is a floor, not a ceiling' framing is now the on-chain consensus. The two suspected attacker addresses are independently verifiable on Cardanoscan, Pool.pm, and Cexplorer — the writer can confirm the 129M ADA figure against the published addresses and against the transaction-flow graph SlowMist has published. Second, the breach is at the wallet-generation layer, not the smart-contract layer. This is structurally distinct from the typical DeFi exploit. If key generation fails, every wallet created through the affected software is at risk — not just the wallets that interacted with a particular contract. The transaction pattern (larger-to-smaller transfers) is consistent with a mnemonic-phrase or private-key batch compromise at the wallet-creation step, which would mean the affected user base is potentially larger than the 178 wallets SecondFi has acknowledged. The Yoroi → SecondFi rebrand (version 10.0.3, shipped 7 June 2026) is the most recent material change to the platform's wallet-generation code; if the vulnerability is in the new code, every wallet created since 7 June 2026 is potentially exposed. If it is in legacy Yoroi code, the exposure is cumulative since 2018. SecondFi has not committed to a timeline for clarifying which. Third, the EMURGO pedigree amplifies the trust damage to the Cardano ecosystem at large. EMURGO is one of the three founding entities of the Cardano blockchain (alongside IOG and the Cardano Foundation). Yoroi was the first Cardano light wallet, launched in 2018, and was the de facto on-ramp for hundreds of thousands of ADA holders. A breach at the wallet-generation layer at an EMURGO-launched platform is a Cardano-ecosystem-level event, not an isolated vendor incident — but as of publication, neither the Cardano Foundation nor IOG has issued a statement on the breach. The structural fingerprint is identical to the T1 Energy / Trina Solar / FEOC pattern (16 June, executive understates scale, third-party investigator produces larger number) and the WiseTech / Richard White / AFP visa-probe pattern (23 June, executive understates severity, third-party investigation produces substantively different framing). The pattern is: official disclosure understates → third-party forensic review produces larger number → official position is 'audit is incomplete, no comment' → the on-chain record (or the FOIA document, or the dated invoice chain) is the primary evidence. The article's distinguishing finding is the specific wallet-generation layer breach, the specific EMURGO-Cardano-ecosystem governance event framing, and the specific SlowMist-on-chain-129M-ADA figure that elevates this from the prior corporate-disclosure cluster.
verdict: The SecondFi / Yoroi breach is the third markets-finance / corporate-disclosure archetype in the Siphoned Truth beat cluster, after T1 Energy / Trina Solar (16 June) and WiseTech / Richard White (23 June). What makes this one beat-distinct is the specific wallet-generation-layer breach (distinct from smart-contract exploits — affects every wallet created through the affected software, not just contract interactions), the specific 8x gap between SecondFi's $2.4M / 16M ADA official figure and SlowMist's $20M / 129M ADA independent figure, the specific EMURGO pedigree amplifying the trust damage to the Cardano ecosystem, and the specific compensation-plan and forensic-review timing gaps that the prior two corporate-disclosure stories did not contain. The recommendation to the writer is to quote SlowMist's X thread verbatim, to verify the two suspected attacker addresses via independent on-chain explorers (Cardanoscan / Pool.pm / Cexplorer) to confirm the 129M ADA figure, to flag the EMURGO relationship as a Cardano-ecosystem governance event, and to note the compensation-plan gap as the unresolved disclosure question. The risk of speculation is on whether the breach was internal vs external — SlowMist's 'batch of mnemonic phrases' framing is consistent with multiple causes and the article should not assert a single cause. The load-bearing question is whether the vulnerability is in the 10.0.3 rebrand code (post-7 June 2026 exposure) or in legacy Yoroi code (cumulative since 2018 exposure), and the size of the compensation pool SecondFi will commit to. As of publication, SecondFi has not committed to a timeline for either clarification.
